name: Valle de la Serena – Republican defence line (La Serena pocket)
story: From late 1936 the Republic held a large salient in eastern Badajoz, the 'La Serena pocket'. Along the Guadámez valley Republican engineers and local masons built concrete-and-brick machine-gun posts linked by zigzag trenches; one carries the inscription 'AÑO 1937'. In July 1938 Queipo de Llano's Army of the South attacked, taking Castuera, Campanario and Villanueva de la Serena and cutting off much of the pocket, while the Republican front fell back to the Zújar and Guadiana. Unlike the famous fronts, these works are almost untouched and little visited.
see: Small round and square fortines (about 3 × 3 m inside, four firing slits) and stretches of trench at Cañada Honda and Los Palancares, controlling the roads to Puebla de la Reina and Don Benito.
plan: On farmland off local roads; no signage — go with a local guide or the 'guerracivilenbadajoz' route notes, wear boots, respect livestock gates. The pin marks the town: ask locally for the exact spot.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
